title: Power Automate: AI-assisted UI automation repair in the desktop flow designer
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap details, designer repair workflow, preview licensing and cited control are supported. The changed runtime repair, self-healing and governance pages do not contradict its claims; it appropriately distinguishes designer repair from runtime repair and reports Microsoft's conflicting control-scope guidance.

claims.claim: In the desktop flow designer, the maker selects Run with AI-assisted UI Automation Repair to start the feature.
claims.quote: In the flow designer, select the option **Run with AI-assisted UI Automation Repair** to start debugging the flow with the AI system's assistance.

claims.claim: A repair dialog opens while the flow runs.
claims.quote: The new dialog interface that appears walks you through the AI system's steps when the flow run goes through actions that reference UI elements, validating their selector.

claims.claim: The repair interface validates each selector used in the flow.
claims.quote: The UI automation repair interface launches while the flow is running, validating each selector used in the flow.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After an eligible selector failure, the system prompts the maker to capture the intended element.
claims.quote: When an eligible selector-related failure occurs, the system prompts you to capture the target element and its current selector.

claims.claim: The system proposes a new selector after the maker recaptures the element.
claims.quote:
The maker recaptures the intended UI element.
3. The system analyzes the failing selector and the newly captured selector.
4. AI generates a suggested selector designed to be more resilient.

claims.claim: The maker can review, edit and test the proposed selector.
claims.quote: Review, edit, and test the proposed selector.

claims.claim: The maker can accept the selector, recapture the element or skip the suggestion.
claims.quote: Accept the selector, recapture the UI element to repeat the process, or skip the suggestion.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents AI-assisted UI automation repair as a preview feature.
claims.quote:
# AI-assisted UI automation repair (preview)

[This topic is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

Important

This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The feature requires Power Automate for desktop version 2.70 or higher.
claims.quote: You need version 2.70 or higher for Power Automate for desktop.

claims.claim: Application or web-page changes and broken selectors can cause UI automation failures.
claims.quote:
Desktop applications or web pages change their UI structure.
- Existing selectors no longer uniquely identify the intended element.
- UI or browser automation actions start failing with *Element not found* errors.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The feature analyzes the failing selector together with a newly captured selector of the same UI element.
claims.quote: the feature analyzes the failing selector together with a newly captured selector of the same UI element and proposes a more resilient selector that makers can review, test, and apply.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Selector changes made during an AI-assisted run become permanent when the maker saves the flow.
claims.quote: The changes are permanently saved when you save the flow, as is the case with any other edits in the flow.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: AI-assisted repair is available only through the desktop flow designer during debugging, not attended or unattended runtime execution.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair is a debugging capability, available only through the flow designer. It doesn't automatically repair selectors during unattended or attended runtime execution.

claims.claim: No new identity or permission model is described for AI-assisted designer repair.
claims.quote: Searched: AI-assisted UI automation repair default disable permission identity; read the repair article and desktop Copilot and governance pages. No new identity or permission model for designer repair was stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Selector changes require user review and approval before application.
claims.quote:
Requires user review and approval before it applies selector changes.
- Doesn't automatically modify flows without user interaction.

claims.claim: Skipping a suggestion without error handling stops the AI-assisted debugging run.
claims.quote: If you skip the suggestion and no error handling is in place, the run throws an error and the AI-assisted debugging run stops.

claims.claim: Accepting a selector updates the affected action and changes the selectors used by the flow.
claims.quote: If the maker accepts the suggested selector, it's added to the selectors list of the affected element, so that the action is updated accordingly and the flow can continue to run.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: AI-assisted designer repair requires the shared Copilot in Power Automate setting.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair relies on generative AI models and requires the same Copilot prerequisite as other AI-powered capabilities in Power Automate:

claims.claim: The repair article gives Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Automate > Copilot in Power Automate > On.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to [Copilot > Settings](https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com/copilot/settings). Under the Power Automate section, select **Copilot in Power Automate**, and then enable the **On** check box in the displayed pane.

claims.claim: The Copilot hub describes these controls as configurable at environment level, with most also configurable through environment groups.
claims.quote: You can configure settings at the environment level, with most settings also configurable through environment groups and rules.

claims.claim: No API equivalent is documented for the environment Copilot setting required by AI-assisted designer repair.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot in Power Automate Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell settings; Copilot in Power Automate Set-TenantSettings API enable disable. Read repair, list-tenantsettings and pac admin excerpts; disableCopilot is documented for cloud flows, not this environment control.

claims.where: controls[1].ui, controls[1].api; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate administrative switch or maker-group switch specific to AI-assisted designer repair is documented on either UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: AI-assisted UI automation repair admin configuration switch API Dataverse table; AI-assisted UI automation repair licensing general availability price admin disable switch. Read repair, governance, tenant settings and Copilot hub; no dedicated admin or maker-group switch found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The initial state of the feature's required environment setting is not stated, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: AI-assisted UI automation repair default disable permission identity; Copilot in Power Automate environment setting default enabled. Read repair and Copilot hub; neither gives this environment setting's initial state. Overview gives a tenant default and denies environment support.

claims.claim: The broader Copilot in Power Automate overview says Copilot is on by default.
claims.quote: If a region has GPUs (UK, Australia, US, India), Microsoft turns on Copilot by default.

claims.claim: The overview describes disabling Copilot at tenant level and explicitly says environment-level support is unavailable, unlike the Copilot hub.
claims.quote: an admin needs to contact support and they use a PowerShell script to turn it off only at tenant level. Environment level support isn't available.

claims.claim: Other desktop Copilot preview capabilities have documented regional and account-type restrictions.
claims.quote:
Create flows using Copilot (preview)
    - United States

Currently, Copilot in Power Automate for desktop is only available for users with a work or school account.

claims.claim: Microsoft's desktop governance page directs administrators to Microsoft Customer Support to disable all Copilot functionality.
claims.quote: To prevent your users from using any copilot capability contact Microsoft Customer Support to disable all copilot functionality in your tenant.

claims.claim: Runtime repair has its own configuration.
claims.quote: Find the **Repair at runtime** setting for the desired run mode (`attended` and `unattended`) under the **Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration** setting in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The overview says Copilot in regions without GPUs depends on cross-geo data sharing.
claims.quote: If a region doesn't have GPUs (everywhere else except sovereign clouds), Microsoft turns on Copilot by default by toggling on the cross-geo data sharing.

claims.claim: The desktop Copilot page names a Copilot feedback tenant setting.
claims.quote: you can prevent users from sending Copilot feedback to Microsoft by using the "Copilot feedback" [tenant setting](/en-us/power-platform/admin/tenant-settings).

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state that Copilot feedback and disableSurveyFeedback are the same setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot feedback disableSurveyFeedback. Read desktop Copilot, governance, tenant-settings and list-tenantsettings. The latter describes disableSurveyFeedback as NPS survey prompts and separately lists disableCopilotFeedback; no equivalence is stated.

claims.claim: Self-healing has a separate per-action setting.
claims.quote:
Enable self-healing per action:

    - Select a supported UI or browser automation action in the flow designer.

    - Open the **Error handling** settings.
    - Turn on **Self-healing (Preview)**.

claims.claim: The desktop governance page names disableSurveyFeedback for preventing Copilot-related feedback.
claims.quote: As a Power Platform admin you can prevent users from sending feedback to Microsoft by disabling the `disableSurveyFeedback` tenant setting.

controlChecks.governs: Copilot in Power Automate for an environment
